view-01.png.evidence: Mottled olive ground, shoreline boulders and dark hangar sides give more surface variety; runway remains readable but ground still resembles a broad blurred texture.

view-02.png.evidence: Deck has alternating plank-like strips and darker surrounding hull, with a visible long wake; narrow tan deck separates less strongly from the sea than the pale full-width deck in view-12.

view-03.png.evidence: Busy carrier scene shows varied deck strips and white bow foam; lighter aircraft shadows avoid some dark duplicates, though overlapping wings and spark dots still hide the player.

view-04.png.evidence: Crisp roof frames, runway, shoreline rocks and tree shadows give physical structure; broad grass is still flat despite visible tracks.

view-05.png.evidence: Crisp hangars and runway sit on visibly varied olive grass with boulders and sand transition; surface variation adds richness without convincing small-scale material lighting.

view-06.png.evidence: Market stalls separate produce, stone, wood and fabric with coherent light and cast shadows; thin tactical paths remain visible through a dense crowd.

view-07.png.evidence: Explosion contains layered rays, sparks and bloom against complex machinery and atmospheric cliffs; intense light and overlapping units reduce local silhouette clarity.

view-08.png.evidence: Shoreline stones and deeper tree/building shadows give volume; fields remain plain patches and smooth sea/grass look schematic.

view-09.png.evidence: Olive grass has mottled variation and field rows are visible; rocks and cast shadows enrich the coast, but scenery remains soft with limited material distinction.

view-10.png.evidence: Boulders and tree shadows provide depth around a readable base; roof, grass and road surfaces have modest differentiation and soft edges.

view-11.png.evidence: Sharper trees, stones and hangar edges combine with olive ground variation and subtle field rows; water flecks add activity but look detached from waves.

view-12.png.evidence: Raised bridge and shadows help height in a clear quiet frame; deck is broad and flat, water is soft, and no developed trailing wake is visible.

view-13.png.evidence: Planked deck, bright bow foam and trailing wake enrich the crowded carrier; sharper wings and lighter shadows help relative separation, but many identical planes still overlap.

view-14.png.evidence: Sharper deck strips, hull edge and visible wake improve carrier form and effects; darkened outer hull blends into teal water and aircraft pile up at the near end.

view-15.png.evidence: Cutaway rooms show consistent warm/cool illumination, wall depth, textured floors and furniture; tactical symbols stay distinguishable within rich environmental detail.

view-16.png.evidence: Visible deck strips and long ship wake add material/effect interest; soft aircraft edges and muted hull-water contrast limit clarity.

view-17.png.evidence: Strong tree/hangar shadows and shoreline boulders ground the coast; large fields remain smooth rectangular patches beside sparse water flecks.

view-18.png.evidence: Directional plane shadows add depth but multiply dark silhouettes around the crowded carrier; cream wings, soft dots and whitecaps compete at the center.

view-19.png.evidence: Layered fog, autumn trees, muddy ruts and weathered shed establish rich depth; smoke and fire integrate well but gray tanks blend with terrain.

view-20.png.evidence: Crisp rails and raised carrier bridge give a clear shape and volume; flat deck materials and absent long wake limit finish.

view-21.png.evidence: Soft planes and offset dark shadows create a dense swarm around flat deck; spark dots make the central player harder to isolate.

view-22.png.evidence: Directional shadows establish aircraft height, with clear top HUD; soft rendering, flat deck and weak wake hold back depth and effects.

view-23.png.evidence: Sharp aircraft and elevated bridge give more form, but heavy dark duplicate shadows and missing long wake reduce polish.

view-24.png.evidence: Wet reflections, rain, smoke volume and orange tracer integrate convincingly; small dark troops are difficult to distinguish at phone scale.

view-25.png.evidence: Uncluttered carrier shows plank-like strips, dark hull band, bow foam and long wake; realistic metallic response and convincing hull-water contact remain limited.

top3_gaps: Material variation is improving but surfaces still lack convincing physical light response and contact depth.
Crowded carrier scenarios retain severe overlap of similar cream aircraft and soft effects around the player.
Sea highlights, bright bow foam and narrow pale wake need coherent contact with hull and wave direction.
recommendations: Prioritize player separation in crowded frames: preserve a clear silhouette with restrained contrasting outline or local contrast, reduce nearby particle opacity, and keep aircraft shadows subordinate to aircraft.

Add scale-appropriate material detail and directional response to hangar roofs, carrier hull and runway: subtle panel seams, edge highlights, contact occlusion and localized wear rather than more broad color noise.

Build the hull-water contact as one integrated effect: thin edge foam following the hull, a widening translucent wake and a few directional foam streaks matching wave scale; tone down isolated white fragments.

Make land feel specific through a small amount of placed detail: concrete aprons around hangars, dirt transitions at roads, irregular grass wear near structures, and varied shoreline erosion. Preserve the clear runway markings.

visible_regressions.comparison: Compared with pale full-width carrier decks in views 12, 20, 22 and 23, the dark outer hull band lowers carrier-water silhouette contrast. Added material structure is useful, but the edge should remain clear.
New-looking mottled olive ground is richer than smooth green ground but adds broad visual noise; this is a tradeoff, not a major readability regression, and does not yet read as detailed grass.

_summary.blinding_limitations: Every image inspected through view_image. No keys, source, metadata or outside files opened. Repeated controls and reference compositions are visually recognizable from prior packets; their established score vectors are preserved. Comparisons are based on visible appearance, not inferred iteration names.
